intro.title: break-inside and pagination
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-column article layout that demonstrates how to control where content breaks across pages or columns. You will learn the core CSS concept of the 'break-inside' property to prevent unwanted splits in elements like images or paragraphs. The main technologies involved are CSS properties for pagination and column layout, specifically 'break-inside' and 'column-count'. By the end, you'll understand how to use these properties to create cleaner, more readable printed or multi-column web content.
intro.usecase: The break-inside property is essential for creating professional print-ready documents and multi-column layouts that maintain readability across page breaks. Developers use it in dashboard reporting tools to prevent charts and data tables from being awkwardly split between printed pages. E-commerce platforms apply break-inside to product catalogs and invoices, ensuring product descriptions and pricing tables stay intact when customers print receipts. Content management systems also utilize this property for articles and documentation, keeping code examples and images together in multi-column magazine-style layouts.
